Petra Diamonds expects its shares to be suspended from 2 November, after missing its 31 October filing deadline. The London-listed miner's FY2026 audit is unfinished, and it offers no certainty on when trading would resume, per its own filing. The delay follows a UK court's 19 October wind-up of a Petra treasury unit over a separate £5.65 million tax claim.

Chow Tai Fook says half-year profit could rise 90 to 100%, and names a gold-loan contract gain as the alert's first reason. Core-market sales improvement is named second; group retail value actually fell 0.5% in the July-to-September quarter, with mainland China down 5.3% against Hong Kong, Macau and other markets up 33.2%, per RTHK.
